Today the firm operates as a full contract manufacturer specializing in custom plastic injection molding. Its capabilities span product design, tooling and automation, molding assembly, transfer programs, fulfillment services, and assembly and decorating. The company emphasizes a concept-to-completion approach, investing in modern equipment and trained personnel to handle complex parts and diverse materials.

Molding Services serves customers worldwide across a range of industries, though the company does not publicly list specific sectors. Its client base includes corporations seeking customized plastic components and assemblies, with the company positioning itself as a single-source partner for design, molding, and post-molding operations.

The company traces its origin to a desire to let clients focus on selling while it handled manufacturing. It cites its proven processes, continuous improvement program targeting productivity and cost effectiveness, and a commitment to treating each project as its own as key differentiators.

old_description: Montana Auto & Fabrication is a complete custom fabrication shop. The company began operations in 2008 and has established itself as a custom off road vehicle shop. Our goal is to take an idea and make it a reality. We are always looking for new projects. Follow us on social media to see our latest work!
about:
Montana Auto & Fabrication operates from Helena, Montana, where it was founded in 2008 by Ryan Weber. Weber purchased Rocky Mountain Radiator that same year and launched the fabrication business alongside it, aiming to turn custom concepts into finished metalwork.

The shop handles a wide range of fabrication tasks, from complete off‑road vehicle builds to partial modifications such as axle swaps, gear setups, lift kits, and custom bumpers and fenders. Beyond automotive work, the team produces custom signage, brewery piping, railings, and sandblasted components for residential and commercial clients. A small crew of fabricators and technicians works with aluminum, stainless steel, and mild steel to deliver one‑off parts and small‑batch projects.

Customers include off‑road enthusiasts building rigs like the Toyota FJ80 and FJ40, breweries needing stainless staircases, canning‑line platforms, and mill‑room adapters, as well as businesses and homeowners requiring custom metalwork. The company also stocks and installs parts from a long list of off‑road brands such as Rough Country, ARB, and Warn.

Weber says the business was started to “take an idea and make it a reality,” emphasizing a willingness to tackle projects of any size. Testimonials highlight on‑time delivery, fair pricing, and a focus on quality craftsmanship across materials and applications.

name: Montana Precision Products
old_description: Montana Precision Products, a joint venture between SeaCast, Inc. and GE Aviation, was founded in 2012 and currently employs about 190 people. MPP specializes in welded tube/duct assemblies and structural castings for aerospace and commercial applications.
about:
Montana Precision Products operates from Butte, Montana, where it was established in 2012 as a joint venture between SeaCast, Inc. and GE Aviation. The partnership combined SeaCast's investment casting expertise with GE Aviation's aerospace engineering resources to serve the commercial and defense aviation markets.

The company produces welded tube and duct assemblies, small structural investment castings, and a newer line of flex joints designed to absorb thermal expansion and vibration in engine and airframe ducting systems. Its 97,000-square-foot facility houses vacuum and air melt furnaces for nickel super alloys, stainless and alloy steels, and cobalt alloys, along with 4-axis CNC machining centers, a horizontal turning center, and a range of welding and tube-forming equipment. About 190 employees work across two shifts, handling everything from melt chemical analysis to final inspection.

MPP's customer base centers on the aerospace sector, supplying net-shape castings and welded assemblies for commercial and military engine programs. The flex joints product line, launched after the 2022 expansion, targets engine and aircraft ducting systems where movement absorption is critical. The company also serves commercial applications that require high-integrity metal components.

Leadership emphasizes a mission built on teamwork, technical innovation, and continual improvement to deliver net-shape castings and welded assemblies. The 2022 expansion added 56,000 square feet specifically to launch the flex joints line, which the board chairman described as a significant engineering and operational achievement that strengthens MPP's role in the international aerospace supply chain.

name: Morton Solar, LLC
old_description: Industrial Control Engineering, LLC was founded by Brad Morton after spending several years in the automated manufacturing industry as a Controls Engineer.  The primary customer was the Caterpillar Mining Truck Plant in Decatur, Illinois where Brad design and programmed several automated manufacturing machines for wheel and drivetrain components of Caterpillar’s mining truck product line.  One truck in particular was the CAT 797 which at one point was the largest mining truck in the world.  This business supported many of the early efforts to educate and promote solar energy.
about:
Morton Solar, LLC was founded in 2006 by Brad Morton in Evansville, Indiana. After years as a controls engineer at Caterpillar's mining truck plant in Decatur, Illinois, where he designed automated machinery for the CAT 797 mining truck, Morton established the company to advance solar energy adoption in the tri-state region.

The firm operates as a full-service solar and electrical contractor, delivering engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) for residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, and utility-scale photovoltaic systems. It also installs battery energy storage systems, including Tesla Powerwall and commercial BESS, EV charging infrastructure, and provides commercial and industrial electrical contracting through its parent company, Morton Electric, covering automation and controls, power distribution, panel building, and advanced manufacturing support. Notable installations include a 1.4 MW system for Vuteq in Princeton, a 2 MW array for AstraZeneca in Mount Vernon, and a 540 kW solar canopy for Orthopaedic Associates in Newburgh.

Morton Solar serves homeowners, businesses, farms, nonprofits, municipalities, schools, medical facilities, and industrial manufacturers across southern Indiana, western Kentucky, and southeastern Illinois. Its public-sector portfolio includes two of the nation's first net-zero energy public buildings—Richardsville Elementary School and Chrisney Library—as well as projects for utilities and government agencies.

The company distinguishes itself through a values-driven model, holding B Corp certification and membership in the Amicus Solar Cooperative. Its team includes NABCEP-certified professionals and an in-house grant writer for USDA REAP grants, and it is an approved SREC vendor for the Illinois Shines program. Morton Solar has also advocated for policy changes that expanded net-metering and streamlined interconnection processes in Indiana.

about:

The company produces custom wood products for the awards, hospitality, and promotional markets, offering services that span CNC machining, printing and engraving, bundling and kitting, and third‑party logistics including warehousing, pick‑and‑pack, labeling, and direct shipping. With a daily output exceeding 7,000 units and more than 2.5 million projects completed, Moslow serves over 600 active clients each month from its Virginia facility.

Its customer base spans the awards and recognition, hospitality and foodservice, and promotional and corporate gifting sectors. The company works with national brands that require custom‑crafted wooden items such as awards, signage, and promotional gifts, delivering them through integrated design, production, and fulfillment workflows.

Moslow emphasizes its century‑plus legacy, American‑made production, and a commitment to rapid response that it says makes it one of the industry’s largest U.S. suppliers. The firm cites a 97 % on‑time delivery rate, 98 % customer satisfaction, and rush‑order turnaround 80 % faster than the industry average as evidence of its reliability.

name: Mountain Meadow Wool Mill
old_description: Founded in 2007 by Karen Hostetler, the mill was born from a mission to preserve the ranching culture of the Great American West. Over a century ago, Basque sheepherders settled Wyoming, establishing small ranches in the late 1800s. However, declining wool prices over the past two decades have threatened these historic operations. In 2002, Karen and her partner set out to reverse this trend, opening a full-service mill that offers fair prices to ranchers for their wool.
about:
Mountain Meadow Wool Mill was founded in 2007 by Karen Hostetler in Buffalo, Wyoming. The mill emerged from a mission to preserve the ranching culture of the Great American West, where Basque sheepherders had established small ranches in the late 1800s. Declining wool prices over the preceding decades threatened those operations, prompting Hostetler and her partner to open a full-service mill that would offer fair prices to ranchers for their wool.

The mill handles the entire wool supply chain under one roof: it sources fleece directly from Wyoming ranches, then scours, cards, spins, and knits the fiber into finished goods. Operations include custom processing for outside growers, in-house spinning of yarn, and knitting of apparel, blankets, and home goods. The facility also runs an eco-friendly processing line and maintains a retail shop and wholesale program.

Primary customers are Wyoming sheep ranchers who sell their clip to the mill, as well as wholesale buyers and direct consumers seeking American-made wool yarn, knitting kits, baby blankets, beanies, and wearable art. The mill has supplied fiber for University of Wyoming branded products and collaborates with local artisans through its Legacy Yarn Guild.

Hostetler started the business to reverse the decline of the region’s wool economy and to keep processing jobs in Wyoming. The company emphasizes traceability from ranch to home, fair pricing for producers, and environmentally responsible methods that preserve wool’s natural softness and durability.
